title: The 86% habit of couples who last
lines: Can one tiny habit predict if a couple *lasts*?
Psychologist John Gottman watched newlyweds spend a weekend in a lab apartment.
One partner says, *look at that bird.* That's a bid for attention.
Couples still together years later turned toward those bids *86 percent* of the time.
Be honest: when they point at the bird, do you look up?

title: What holding hands does to your brain
lines: Whose hand calms your brain *the most*?
Researchers warned married women that a small shock might come.
No hand, a stranger's hand, or their *husband's* hand.
Their husband's hand calmed the brain *the most*.
And the happier the couple, the *calmer* it stayed.
So next time you're scared: their hand, or yours?

title: Do couples really start to look alike?
lines: Do couples really start to *look alike*?
A famous 1987 study said yes. So Stanford researchers checked again.
They compared photos of *517 couples*, taken 20 to 69 years apart.
Couples did *not* grow more alike over time.
They already looked similar *from the very start*.
Be honest: do you and your partner look alike?
